facts.statement: Zuniceratops was discovered in 1996 by an eight-year-old boy named Christopher James Wolfe in west-central New Mexico.
facts.quote: Zuniceratops was discovered in 1996 by eight-year-old Christopher James Wolfe, son of paleontologist Douglas G. Wolfe, in the Moreno Hill Formation in west-central New Mexico.

facts.statement: The partial proximal parietal bone of Zuniceratops has an inverted "T" shape, similar to that of Protoceratops.
facts.quote: The partial proximal parietal is shown to have an inverted "T" shape, as in Protoceratops.

facts.statement: While the first discovered specimen had unusual single-rooted teeth, larger fossils show double-rooted teeth, indicating that teeth became double-rooted with age.
facts.quote: Although the first specimen discovered had single-rooted teeth (unusual for ceratopsians), larger fossils had double-rooted teeth, showing that the teeth became double-rooted with age and that it is a plesiomorphic trait.

facts.statement: The genus Zuniceratops contains a single known species, Zuniceratops christopheri.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Zuniceratops christopheri.

facts.statement: Zuniceratops lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now New Mexico, United States.
facts.quote: Zuniceratops ('Zuni horned face') is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaurs that lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: Researchers believe that the brow horns of Zuniceratops would have grown much larger with age.
facts.quote: Se cree que los cuernos de las cejas habrían crecido mucho más con la edad.

facts.statement: The frill of Zuniceratops was a thin, wide structure resembling a shield.
facts.quote: El volante era una estructura delgada, ancha, parecida a un escudo.

facts.statement: The snout of Zuniceratops was long and low, similar to that of chasmosaurines.
facts.quote: El hocico es largo y bajo, como el de los chasmosaurinos.

facts.statement: Zuniceratops was a herbivore like other ceratopsians and was probably an animal that lived in herds.
facts.quote: Zuniceratops era un herbívoro como otros ceratopsios y fue probablemente un animal que vivía en rebaños.

facts.statement: Wolfe and James Kirkland first described Zuniceratops in 1998.
facts.quote: Wolfe y James Kirkland describieron a Zuniceratops por primera vez en 1998.

facts.statement: The name Zuniceratops is derived from the Zuni people of New Mexico and Arizona, who named the basin where fossils were found, and the Latinized Greek term ceratops meaning "horned face".
facts.quote: El nombre se deriva de los Zuñi, un pueblo nativo del sur de Nuevo México y Arizona, que dan nombre a la Cuenca Zuñi donde se hallaron los fósiles, y el término griego latinizado ceratops ("cara con cuerno"), un componente de nombre común en los ceratopsios.

facts.statement: Due to its combination of primitive and advanced features, Zuniceratops is classified as the sister taxon to the family Ceratopsidae, possibly grouped with the Asian ceratopsian Turanoceratops in a group named Ceratopsomorpha by Kirkland and Wolfe.
facts.quote: Dada su combinación de características primitivas y avanzadas, se le clasifica como el taxón hermano de la familia Ceratopsidae, posiblemente junto al ceratopsio asiático Turanoceratops en un grupo al que Kirkland y Wolfe denominaron Ceratopsomorpha.

facts.statement: Zuniceratops lived 10 million years before the family of known horned ceratopsids and provides an important insight into the ancestors of that group.
facts.quote: Vivió 10 millones de años antes de la familia de los conocidos ceratópsidos cornudos y da un importante acercamiento a los ancestros de dicho grupo.

facts.statement: Zuniceratops lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 94 million years ago during the Turonian, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 94 millones de años, durante el Turoniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Zuniceratops is the Turonian stage, from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)
